races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Royal Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 191-day break with well-bred ability but fitness concerns despite impressive debut win
runners_data.comment: Didn't progress after debut win last term; probably best watched on first run for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Well bred (his dam was second in the Oaks), cost 750,000gns as a yearling and made a winning start for Charlie Appleby at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last summer; however, he didn't build on that and he was pulled up in a nursery on his final outing; sold for just 25,000gns in February, gelded and probably best watched on debut for a new stable.

runners_data.name: Vincenzo Peruggia
runners_data.note: Natural leader who will contest early pace, returning from 249-day absence with solid form on softer ground
runners_data.comment: Thrice-raced as 2yo, winning at Beverley; unexposed and commands respect on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Cost 550,000gns as a yearling and ran only three times as a 2yo, winning 7f novice at Beverley (good to firm) before being hampered when last in the Group 2 Vintage Stakes at Goodwood; has not been let in lightly for handicap debut judged on that bare form, but he's completely unexposed, will stay 1m and his stable won this race 12 months ago; respected.

runners_data.name: Kanishka
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent recent form with only 7 days since last run and proven on similar going conditions
runners_data.comment: Arrives after two creditable runs at Southwell; in the mix in first-time cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Arrives on the back of two creditable runs over 7f at Southwell, not beaten far when fourth of nine on latest; should stay 1m and he's at least as effective on turf as AW; in the mix in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Comic Hero
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Oisin Murphy aboard, progressive type who should relish the step up to a mile trip
runners_data.comment: Kempton win last time has been boosted; unexposed; interesting candidate on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent in three runs since debut, gaining a deserved first success at Kempton (7f) in February; the runner-up that day won in clearcut style next time; should be at least as good over 1m and remains unexposed; interesting candidate on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 254-day break after winning his last start but faces fitness test from long absence
runners_data.comment: Progressive last term; Newbury winner on final start; may still have untapped potential
runners_data.spotlight: Improved with each run as a 2yo, readily winning nursery at Newbury (7f, good to firm; subsequently gelded) on last of them in July; has a long absence to overcome but he's in good hands and may still have untapped potential; should have no difficulty at all getting 1m.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: Free-going leader with headgear fitted, recent winner but tendency to race keenly could prove costly
runners_data.comment: 2-3 for George Boughey but mark has risen and others may have more potential
runners_data.spotlight: Free-goer; won his first two races (1m at Kempton and 7f at Wolverhampton) for George Boughey before finishing last of four in the face of a sterner assignment back at Kempton; his mark has risen and others may have more potential.

races.paceDynamic: Vincenzo Peruggia and Utmost Good Faith will clash early as both are confirmed front runners with free-going tendencies. This guaranteed battle will create an honest gallop over the stiff Musselburgh mile, preventing either from getting easy fractions. The three hold-up horses (Kanishka, Comic Hero, Strength Of Spirit) will benefit from tracking behind this pace duel, while prominent racer Monoceros sits in the ideal tactical position. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can capitalize on the expected pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Vincenzo Peruggia and Utmost Good Faith engage in a sustained battle from the start...
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will soften them up for late challengers who can time their runs perfectly. Hold-up horses like Comic Hero and Kanishka are perfectly positioned to exploit the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates Early
scenarios.trigger: If either Vincenzo Peruggia or Utmost Good Faith gets uncontested lead...
scenarios.body: The surviving front runner could dictate fractions and prove hard to peg back, especially if they settle better than expected. Monoceros tracking in second could pose the biggest threat with his prominent style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Monoceros can secure ideal position behind the pace battle...
scenarios.body: His well-bred ability and prominent style could see him strike at the perfect moment when the leaders weaken. The 191-day break remains a concern but class could shine through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Favours Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners settle unexpectedly and create moderate fractions...
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure could allow either Vincenzo Peruggia or Utmost Good Faith to retain enough for the finish. This scenario requires both to show more restraint than their styles suggest.

watchPoints.text: Vincenzo Peruggia and Utmost Good Faith both going too hard early and setting up the race for closers
Monoceros showing any signs of needing the run after his 191-day layoff in the early stages
Comic Hero getting a clean run from his hold-up position as Oisin Murphy times his challenge
Strength Of Spirit overcoming his 254-day absence and showing full fitness from the start
The pace battle intensity in the first half-mile which will determine how the race unfolds

races.name: Livescore Bet Silver Arrow Handicap

runners_data.name: Midnight Gun
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 146 days off, strong jockey booking with James Doyle suggests readiness despite the layoff
runners_data.comment: Strong 7f handicap form when unlucky at Doncaster (soft) in October; solid claims
runners_data.spotlight: Faded in a 1m Listed race at Saint-Cloud (heavy) in November; had previously won a novice and a handicap (good) at that trip but the return to 7f worked well for him at Doncaster (soft) in October when he was bumped and later met trouble, only just failing against one on the crest of a wave; that strong form gives him solid claims.

runners_data.name: Golden Mind
runners_data.note: Can lead if needed but better held up slightly, trainer form poor at 2/22 which is concerning for stable confidence
runners_data.comment: Had a good 2025 with 3 wins at 6f/7f, and smart form in defeat; this sharp test can suit
runners_data.spotlight: Can lead; had some smart form in defeat during 2025 alongside three wins at 6f and 7f (AW and heavy); never showed with a chance on AW comeback but this easy test could see him to advantage; has possibilities.

runners_data.name: Al Arbeed
runners_data.note: Lightly raced prominent runner with Hannon/Levey combination, only 7 days since last run keeps him sharp
runners_data.comment: Useful 7f form in warm Southwell handicap over 7f; now needs to show he's as good on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Successful 7f debut at Southwell; just a handful of starts since, showing useful form when fourth of ten on handicap debut in a warm race on Southwell AW in October only to run poorly next time; likely to come on for last week's Kempton run but now needs to show he can hack it on turf.

runners_data.name: Gweedore
runners_data.note: Course specialist with 6 wins here, prominent style suits but 9-year-old legs may not have same turn of foot
runners_data.comment: Six course wins, the latest over C&D in November; same mark as 2nd in this race last year
runners_data.spotlight: Often leads; superb 9yo with six course wins, the latest over C&D (soft) in November; not weighted out of it off the same mark as his second to Persuasion here last April but he's had a much longer break this time and is drawn widest.

runners_data.name: Persuasion
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won this race last year, back below that winning mark creates opportunity
runners_data.comment: Won this on his course debut last year; below that mark now; this should take more winning
runners_data.spotlight: Five wins include this race on course debut (good to soft) last year, when beating Gweedore; back below that winning mark but today's race should take more winning and he'll do well to make it three wins in the last four runnings for his yard.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Better on faster ground historically, prominent style may get caught in traffic problems
runners_data.comment: Two Listed AW wins (7f/6f); cosy turf winner on good to firm in August; ground query today
runners_data.spotlight: Made his name on AW but he can do it on turf when the ground is quick, as when a cosy winner at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) in August; has since added a second Listed AW event, at Southwell in November, but the Saudi Arabia venture came to nothing in February and he has ground worries today.

runners_data.name: A War Eagle
runners_data.note: Returning after 193 days off with 7lb claimer, eased when meeting soft ground last time suggests going concern
runners_data.comment: Mildly progressive in handicaps as 3yo; sold from E Bethell for 26,000gns; check market
runners_data.spotlight: Eased right down when switched to soft ground on final 3yo start but mildly progressive in handicaps at about this trip previously, his win coming at Beverley (good to firm) last June; left Edward Bethell for 26,000gns in the autumn; 2lb out of the weights but worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong course form, 7 wins in 2025 shows she's in career-best form
runners_data.comment: Seven wins for new yard in 2025, at 6f-1m;; needs to be better than ever for a win today
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins in 2025, at 6f-1m on ground ranging from good to firm to soft, including one over C&D; however, she was beaten three times off this mark since the latest of them in September so needs to be better than ever to have a chance of making a winning reappearance.

runners_data.name: Bellarchi
runners_data.note: Beat Jannas Journey over course and distance in October, subsequent poor runs suggest that was her peak effort
runners_data.comment: Made it 2-3 over C&D in October; much lesser efforts since; easier targets await
runners_data.spotlight: Has won on good to soft, good to firm and good; made it 2-3 over C&D when beating Jannas Journey in October but she was a much lesser light in four subsequent runs last year; made a fair reappearance on AW recently but easier targets await.

runners_data.name: Goldmoyne
runners_data.note: Front-runner on superb streak, only horse guaranteed clear run but soft ground debut unknown
runners_data.comment: Six AW wins at 6f-1m for this yard; has a very different task now back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: On lowly mark when arriving at this yard but he's found new reserves as the AW season has gone on and was winning for the sixth time when completing a front-running four-timer at Lingfield (1m; earlier wins at 6f/7f) recently; acted on turf in modest company in Ireland but this is more problematic.

races.paceDynamic: Goldmoyne will lead from the gate and set a steady tempo on the soft ground, with no other dedicated front-runners to pressure him early. The main tactical battle develops behind as Golden Mind, Midnight Gun, Al Arbeed, Gweedore, and Royal Zabeel all want prominent positions, creating a cluster 2-3 lengths off the leader. This congestion will cause traffic problems turning for home as five horses fight for racing room. The combination of uncontested early leader and prominent bottleneck strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay wide and make late moves.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group gets tangled up turning for home and blocks each other
scenarios.body: Persuasion and Jannas Journey get clear runs down the outside while the prominent runners interfere with each other. Their patient tactics and strong finishing kicks prove decisive in the soft conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Goldmoyne wires field
scenarios.trigger: If Goldmoyne's recent winning streak continues and he kicks clear approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: His uncontested lead allows him to find another gear when challenged, similar to his recent AW victories. The soft ground doesn't stop his momentum as the prominent pack arrives too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent group breaks clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners gets first run on Goldmoyne and the others follow through cleanly
scenarios.body: Midnight Gun or Golden Mind times their move perfectly to collar the leader while avoiding the traffic behind. Their class tells in a driving finish with the early leader still clinging on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Goldmoyne stops suddenly and the prominent group also fades after their early exertions
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between the hold-up horses who have conserved energy. Bellarchi or A War Eagle could emerge from the pack in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Goldmoyne's early fractions - if he goes too fast trying to put the race to bed, he'll tie up in the soft ground
Monitor the prominent group at the 3f marker - if Golden Mind, Midnight Gun, Al Arbeed, Gweedore and Royal Zabeel are all bunched together, expect major traffic problems
Check if Persuasion gets her preferred position tracking wide in rear - her hold-up style needs room to maneuver late
Observe A War Eagle's action on the soft surface - was eased last time on similar going which suggests he may not handle it
Watch for early market moves on Midnight Gun given the long absence and strong jockey booking combination

races.name: Virgin Bet Goliath Cup Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Al Qareem
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 168 days off but has strong course form and Burke's stable is hitting form with 2 winners from 19 runners recently
runners_data.comment: Has never won first time out but he has run creditably and is the clear form pick
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who keeps pulling out more, with 12 wins; the four last season (April-October) included career-best form; unraced here; has never won first time out but he has run creditably and is the clear form pick.

runners_data.name: Mount Atlas
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse ideally suited to this distance with Oisin Murphy's timing crucial, though 161 days since last run is a slight concern
runners_data.comment: Solid campaign last season but there's a bit for him to prove on this first crack at 1m6f
runners_data.spotlight: Had a very solid campaign last season bar one blip (front-running was blamed); all but one of those races was at 1m4f, with a creditable fifth of six thrown in over the extended 1m5f at Chester in May (Group 3) but there is a bit for him to prove on this first foray over 1m6f.

runners_data.name: Roaring Legend
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who underwent wind surgery and showed improvement in recent Wolverhampton runs, only 36 days since last outing keeps him sharp
runners_data.comment: Never better than in February; peak turf form not far behind; probably be on the premises
runners_data.spotlight: A poor show last May prompted a second wind operation and it was a solid campaign otherwise; never better than when second this February in 2m AW handicaps at Wolverhampton and Lingfield, but peak turf form isn't far behind it and he'll probably be on the premises.

runners_data.name: Lady Vivian
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up significantly in class after 185-day break, though Ralph Beckett stable struggling with just 0 from 8 in past 14 days
runners_data.comment: 2nd from off the pace at Toulouse (Listed) on final start gave hope for this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden and front-running handicap winner last spring, who found her one Group and two Listed assignments much harder afterwards but those were her best form; all those were at about 1m4f but her second from off the pace at Toulouse on final outing gave hope for this longer trip; improvement needed.

runners_data.name: Kate O'Riley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching from hurdles back to Flat with just 31 days since last run, but significant class rise from AW handicaps to Listed company
runners_data.comment: More to prove on Flat turf and over new trip, with a big step forward required anyway
runners_data.spotlight: Dual Wolverhampton AW winner (8.5f/1m4f) for Michael Bell, a hurdles winner in October and back on the Flat with two good AW runs (1m2f/1m3f handicaps) this year; has a bit more to prove as turf performer on the Flat and also over this new trip, with a big step forward required at this level.

runners_data.name: Many Men
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent 1m6f form but returning after 183 days off, though Jim Boyle's small string shows good strike rate at 2 from 5 recently
runners_data.comment: Better still is required but his record of improvement demands respect
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent progress included three handicap wins (1m2f, 1m6f and 2m) last March-July and an agonisingly close call in the Melrose at York in August; close fourth in 1m6f Listed race at Ascot on final outing; better still is required but his record of improvement demands respect.

races.paceDynamic: Roaring Legend will lead from the start with no genuine pace pressure, as Al Qareem and Lady Vivian prefer prominent positions rather than forcing the issue early. The confirmed front-runner can dictate a comfortable gallop over this stamina-testing 1m6f trip on good to soft ground. With Mount Atlas, Kate O'Riley, and Many Men all hold-up horses needing the race to develop, they'll be tracking a measured pace before unleashing their finishing kicks. This sustainable pace scenario clearly favours the hold-up horses who can time their runs perfectly off an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Legend sets an uncontested lead allowing closers to strike
scenarios.body: The front-runner's comfortable gallop plays into the hands of the three quality hold-up performers who can unleash devastating finishing kicks. Mount Atlas and Many Men have both shown excellent closing ability at this distance previously.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Legend maintains enough stamina reserves to resist late challenges
scenarios.body: The recent wind operation has improved his breathing and he gets the perfect scenario to utilise his tactical speed advantage. His two recent seconds at Wolverhampton showed renewed vigor over similar distances.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Times It
scenarios.trigger: If Al Qareem or Lady Vivian can position perfectly behind the leader and outkick the field
scenarios.body: Either prominent runner avoids the traffic issues that could hamper the hold-up brigade while staying close enough to the pace. Al Qareem's front-running tendencies could see him press Roaring Legend and take over late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Legend goes too slowly and the race becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The crawling pace allows every horse to remain competitive turning for home, creating a messy finish where class tells. The highest-rated horses with tactical speed would benefit most from this lottery scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Roaring Legend gets an easy lead early - he could steal a march if allowed to dictate completely uncontested fractions
Monitor Al Qareem's positioning if he decides to press the leader rather than sit prominent, as this could set up the race for closers
Observe Oisin Murphy's tactics on Mount Atlas - his timing from the back will be crucial given the likely slow pace scenario
Check if Lady Vivian can overcome her significant layoff and class rise, as 185 days off is substantial for a Listed race return
Watch Many Men's jumping from hurdles to Flat - Boyle's runners often need their first run back but his recent AW form suggests readiness

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boost Queen's Cup Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Shadow Dance
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 42 days, career best form at these distances but needs to prove handicap value
runners_data.comment: Only mid-division in 2025; rather worse in both runs (first AW races) for new connections
runners_data.spotlight: Career highlights (1m4f/1m6f) for Roger Varian were in 2024 and he managed only mid-division in his three handicaps (at top meetings) last July-September; rather worse in both runs (his first races on AW) for new connections early this year but he returns to turf 8lb below his career-high mark.

runners_data.name: Gambino
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making stable debut for in-form Dan Skelton, good recent form but first time on soft going
runners_data.comment: Seriously unexposed and no great surprise if he starts handicap life on a good mark
runners_data.spotlight: First and second on turf in Ireland last April/August on his only two starts for Noel Meade; debut for new stable saw him take third in the 1m4f AW novice event won by Constitution Hill, followed by another encouraging run on hurdle debut at Newbury two weeks ago; now tongue tied first time; seriously unexposed and no great surprise if he starts handicap life on a good mark.

runners_data.name: Moon Over Miami
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after long absence, perfect at this trip when winning at Newbury last April
runners_data.comment: Off since battling his way to a narrow front-running win at Newbury (2m, good) last April
runners_data.spotlight: Just six races and won his only three on turf; three on AW early last year before he battled his way to a narrow front-running win at Newbury (2m, good) last April; absent since and while he shaped as if he could make into a smart performer, that may be a bit more likely at 2m+.

runners_data.name: Wise Eagle
runners_data.note: Previous course winner who ran well when fourth in this race last year, proven soft ground performer
runners_data.comment: Won this prize in 2023, fourth last year; latest hurdles form was his best in that sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Won this prize in 2023 and had a fruitful Flat/hurdles campaign last winter before his close fourth in this; while he did not make an impact in either of his Flat runs this winter, latest hurdles form was his best in that sphere; 8lb lower than the 2025 renewal and a case can certainly be made.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who found form for James Owen, absent since October but proven at this distance
runners_data.comment: String of creditable efforts over 1m2f-1m4f, but after a lesser effort on sole go at 1m6f
runners_data.spotlight: His only two wins (30 races) were last spring on his first two starts for James Owen; a string of creditable efforts followed over 1m2f-1m4f but that was after a lesser effort on his only attempt at this trip.

runners_data.name: Dancingwithmyself
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course-and-distance win, Michael Bell's 4/7 strike-rate notable
runners_data.comment: Went close on last year's return; clearcut 1m6f win on penultimate start; yard in form
runners_data.spotlight: Not the most consistent but won twice last season, latterly in clearcut fashion with a late bid at Goodwood (1m6f, good to soft) in September despite suffering trouble in running; 6lb higher today but she went close on last year's return and her yard is among the winners on AW; on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner carrying bottom weight with claiming jockey, slow-starting tendency a concern
runners_data.comment: Five-race campaign this winter, when a notch or two below his best; 1-10 record on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Breaking slowly had become a problem (better on latest start) in his five-race campaign this winter, when a notch or two below his best; 1-10 record on turf is also none too persuasive.

runners_data.name: Baileys Khelstar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after long absence, progressive record at these distances when fit
runners_data.comment: Progressive sort as 3yo and early stages as 4yo; unraced since a lesser show in July 2024
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive sort as 3yo and the early stages as 4yo (effective at 1m5f-2m) and he'd be a player if returning in peak form; the potential problem is that he's unraced since a lesser show in July 2024.

runners_data.name: Gentle Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse very reliable in handicaps, won twice at 1m6f last September in quick succession
runners_data.comment: Highly reliable in handicaps, with 1m6f doing the trick for a quick double last September
runners_data.spotlight: Highly reliable in handicaps, with 1m6f doing the trick when he won on good ground at Haydock and Chester in space of a week last September; needs to resume progress but enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Almuhit
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner, returned to form for new stable and will control the tempo
runners_data.comment: Returned to some hurdles form last time; did well last year front-running at 2m on Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Rediscovered the knack for new stable last year, including two Flat wins in four-runner races and two places when the action got more competitive; returned to some hurdles form on latest outing but all last year's achievements came when front-running in 2m races.

runners_data.name: Team Player
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won on stable debut recently, tongue-tie applied for first time worked well
runners_data.comment: Up 5lb but stable debut win (2m, AW) came in tidy style; has to be considered seriously
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice over about 1m4f (good/AW) last summer for Gemma Tutty and, tongue tied for the first time, made a successful stable debut from off the pace in 11-runner race at Newcastle (2m, AW) six weeks ago; up 5lb but that latest win came in tidy style and he has to be considered seriously.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from wind surgery, recent near-miss suggests improvement
runners_data.comment: Back to life for short-head loss over hurdles 13 days ago (second run after wind surgery)
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish; beaten 30l and more over hurdles in first four British starts but back to life for a short-head defeat 13 days ago (second run after wind surgery); now returns to Flat, in which sphere he's 1-9 having won a maiden in 2023 and been second in a 1m5f handicap last July; needs a second look.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Hold-up Musselburgh specialist with excellent course record, cheekpieces applied
runners_data.comment: 2025 wins included three on good ground here in May-October; needs to hit a new high
runners_data.spotlight: Musselburgh specialist (4-10 here) who had three wins at this track on good ground last May-October; also scored at Nottingham in October, a runaway win over 2m2f on heavy going which sees him 5lb higher today; needs to hit a new high and may need to front-run back at this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Almuhit will set the pace uncontested from the front, with Gambino and Sportingsilvermine tracking in prominent positions but neither likely to press early. The sustainable gallop over 1m6f on soft ground will allow the large field of hold-up horses including Moon Over Miami, Wise Eagle, Shadow Dance, and Dancingwithmyself to get into contention. With only one confirmed front-runner and multiple stamina-laden closers, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can unleash late kicks in the final three furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Almuhit sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate
scenarios.body: The patient riders can time their challenges perfectly, with the soft ground aiding stamina over speed. Multiple closers will sweep past the tiring leaders in a cavalry charge finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino or Sportingsilvermine get first run on the turn
scenarios.body: They can steal a march before the hold-up brigade gets organized, with their prominent position giving them tactical advantage. The winner comes from horses positioned third to fifth early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Almuhit Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and no one challenges
scenarios.body: The front-runner can dictate throughout and kick clear when others are still winding up their challenges. His stamina and course experience become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Suits Versatile
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging develops between the prominent runners
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical and favours horses who can adapt to changing pace scenarios. Those with tactical speed from midfield positions benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Almuhit dictating slow fractions early - if unchallenged he could steal a march on the field
Moon Over Miami's fitness after 358 days off - stamina proven but ring-rustiness could blunt finishing kick
Team Player and Mr Lincoln both returning from significant breaks but showing recent form signs
Multiple hold-up horses bunching in behind - traffic problems likely in straight if pace stays steady
Gambino making stable debut for Dan Skelton - market support would indicate immediate readiness

races.name: Virgin Bet Scottish Sprint Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but 175 days off and poor fresh record undermines chances despite reduced mark
runners_data.comment: 16 wins in all but none last season; may be of more interest with a run under his belt
runners_data.spotlight: Successful 16 times in all, seven of those wins coming during a stellar 2024; 0-8 last term, and although his mark has slipped he has no great record fresh and may be of more interest with a run under his belt.

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist perfectly suited if pace collapses, proven course winner and 7lb lower than last success
runners_data.comment: Hasn't won for a while but good third over C&D on 2025 reappearance and now 7lb lower
runners_data.spotlight: A losing sequence is mounting but he has a win and a third from just two attempts over C&D, and the latter was first time out last season; 7lb lower here and he's of obvious interest if cherry ripe after 161 days off (has had wind surgery); one of two very plausible candidates for the Barrons.

runners_data.name: Democracy Dilemma
runners_data.note: Sole front runner conceding weight all round but proven tough 5f specialist who usually dictates
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; respectable third at Lingfield on return; should go well despite topweight
runners_data.spotlight: Tough 5f specialist who usually makes the running; a respectable third at Lingfield six weeks ago should have blown away the cobwebs; concedes weight all round but he's a classy type and should go well.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim
runners_data.note: Prominent type but two poor all-weather runs this term raise fitness concerns despite Royal Ascot success
runners_data.comment: Falling in the weights and a C&D winner; very interesting with good-value claimer booked
runners_data.spotlight: Enjoyed his finest hour when winning the 5f 3yo handicap at Royal Ascot in 2024; seen only twice last season and down the field on both his AW outings this term, but he met trouble last time and is probably in much better form than his finishing position suggests; undoubtedly well handicapped again and this C&D winner is interesting with a good-value claimer booked.

runners_data.name: Rhythm N Hooves
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good recent form, just 14 days since last run gives fitness edge
runners_data.comment: Holding his form well; in the mix but one or two of these could be better handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Prominent racer who won off 2lb lower at Newbury (5f, good to firm) last summer; held his form well without winning on the AW over the winter; no obvious reason why he won't be involved again but one or two of these could be better handicapped.

runners_data.name: Tropical Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 203-day break and gelding operation, hard to assess
runners_data.comment: More miss than hit in 2025 but returns on handy mark after gelding op; big chance
runners_data.spotlight: More miss than hit in 2025, winning 5f Listed race at York (good to firm) in May but failing to make the frame otherwise; now returns from a gelding operation on a handy mark and with his stable in form; big chance if he's on a going day.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Front-running type like stablemate Jordan Electrics but also 175 days off after good 2024 campaign
runners_data.comment: Had excellent 2025, winning the Portland; well drawn if ready to roll after six months off
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; better than ever last season, completing hat-trick in the Portland at Doncaster (extended 5f, good) in September and going close at York (5f, good) the following month; may not have reached her ceiling just yet and well drawn if ready to roll after six months off.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent all-weather form but unproven on turf at this level
runners_data.comment: Three wins at Newcastle but has achieved significantly less in two turf runs
runners_data.spotlight: Scooped a big pot over 7f at Newcastle (200-1) last Easter and has shown even better form over 5f and 6f there since; however, she has achieved significantly less in two turf runs and needs to be right at her best back on grass.

runners_data.name: Vintage Clarets
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who needed his recent comeback run, 3lb lower than last winning mark
runners_data.comment: Ten-time winner; probably needed reappearance; may require another to shake off the rust
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-time winner whose mark is now 3lb lower than for his latest success; probably needed the run when well held at Southwell two weeks ago, but didn't show much and may require another before hitting his stride.

runners_data.name: Lexington Blitz
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for in-form Cowell yard but 161 days off since Catterick success
runners_data.comment: Came good at Catterick last autumn; has since been gelded; not ruled out after a break
runners_data.spotlight: A third representative in this field for Robert Cowell; came good at Catterick (5f, good) last autumn after several near misses; possibly found heavy ground against him at Doncaster on final start and has since been gelded; not ruled out if ready to do himself justice after a break.

runners_data.name: Archduke Ferdinand
runners_data.note: Prominent type making reappearance after 231 days, tough ask in this grade fresh
runners_data.comment: Below par in 2025 after May Redcar win; will have to be in top form after layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Below par in 2025 after winning at Redcar (6f, good to firm) in May; now 1lb lower but this is a warm race for his reappearance and he'll have to be right at the top of his game.

runners_data.name: Against The Wind
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent runner with 14-day fitness advantage and solid recent third at Southwell
runners_data.comment: Personal best with Southwell third; drawn wide but should be in the thick of things again
runners_data.spotlight: Steadily progressive and posted another personal best when third at Southwell (5f, AW) on reappearance; his turf form is at a lower level but he still won at Thirsk last spring and finished third in a big field at York's Dante meeting (both 5f, good to firm); race-fit and should be in the thick of things again if a low draw doesn't count against him.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 182-day break, good course record but needs to be ready
runners_data.comment: Four wins last year and had excuses on last two starts; may still be unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins last year included a 5f Racing League event at Southwell in August, and he didn't get the rub of the green when down the field on his two subsequent starts; may still be unexposed and he's worth a market check after his winter break.

runners_data.name: Gangsta Man
runners_data.note: Prominent type switching from longer trips to sharp 5f, unproven at this distance despite talent
runners_data.comment: Two wins over longer trips in Ireland last year; new yard does very well with sprinters
runners_data.spotlight: Previously trained in Ireland, winning twice (7.5f/7f) in 2025 before changing hands for 31,000gns; has to prove his effectiveness over a sharp 5f, although his new stable does have a tremendous knack with sprinters.

races.paceDynamic: Democracy Dilemma will take them along at a steady tempo as the sole confirmed leader, but faces immediate pressure from six prominent racers including Eternal Sunshine, Rhythm N Hooves, and Pilgrim all wanting to sit close. This creates a bunched field through the early stages with genuine pace pressure building from 2f out as the prominent brigade fan out. The combination of tactical speed and multiple prominent runners closing on a single leader heavily favours horses that can either sustain from the front or deliver late kicks from hold-up positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Democracy Dilemma gets an uncontested lead and the prominent pack hesitates
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too honest for chasers as Democracy Dilemma kicks clear turning for home, with late closers unable to bridge the gap on testing ground. Rhythm N Hooves and Eternal Sunshine battle for the minors but can't catch the winner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack goes too hard chasing Democracy Dilemma through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The early pace becomes unsustainable as multiple prominent runners clash, setting up perfectly for Jer Batt and Vintage Clarets to deliver telling late charges. The hold-up pair benefit from the collapse ahead and superior finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner positions perfectly behind Democracy Dilemma without getting caught in traffic
scenarios.body: Rhythm N Hooves or Against The Wind gets first run on the leader approaching the final furlong, having avoided the scrimmaging behind. Their tactical positioning and race fitness proves decisive over both the tiring leader and unlucky traffic-hit rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Democracy Dilemma goes too slow early then multiple prominent runners surge simultaneously
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint from 2f out with no clear pace advantage, allowing an outsider like Tropical Storm to benefit from the chaos with fresh legs after his break. The form horses all compromise each other in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Traffic chaos likely from 2f out as six prominent runners including Rhythm N Hooves, Pilgrim and Against The Wind converge behind Democracy Dilemma
Democracy Dilemma's stamina reserves under pressure conceding weight to entire field while setting honest pace
Jer Batt needs clear late run from back of field - any interference in straight compromises main winning chance
Robert Cowell trio of Democracy Dilemma, Rhythm N Hooves and Lexington Blitz suggests yard expects big run from one
Both Goldie runners Jordan Electrics and Eternal Sunshine returning from 175-day breaks, monitor market support for stable confidence

races.name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Adonius
runners_data.comment: £32,000 yearling by Soldier's Call; stable has a modest strike-rate with 2yos
runners_data.spotlight: £32,000 yearling; Soldier's Call half-brother to winners Golden Paradise (5f 2yo; RPR 71) and For Fake (Italian 5f-6f 2yo); dam placed four times at 5f (65), half-sister to winners Mother Country (7f/1m) and Banddar (5f 2yo); already gelded; stable has a modest strike-rate with 2yos.

runners_data.name: River Jordan
runners_data.comment: £9,000 yearling; drawn on the rail; yard 8-100 with 2yos in last five seasons
runners_data.spotlight: £9,000 yearling; Ubettabelieveit half-brother to winners Evening Song (6f-1m1f including 2yo; RPR 77), Offiah's Boy (1m2f/11.6f; 64) and Larrsen (1m; 61); drawn on the rail; yard 8-100 with 2yos in last five seasons.

runners_data.name: Super Alpha
runners_data.comment: 45,000euros yearling; by Bated Breath; fits the bill on pedigree; interesting newcomer
runners_data.spotlight: 45,000euros yearling; by Bated Breath; brother to 6f 2yo winner Juliet Sierra (including Group 3; RPR 98), closely related to two winners including Juliet Foxtrot (7f-9.5f including 2yo/US Grade 1; 109), half-brother to four winners; dam 7.5f/1m winner (including 2yo/Listed; 106); fits the bill on pedigree; interesting newcomer.

runners_data.name: Jaydee's Dream
runners_data.comment: 13,000euros yearling; pedigree suggests he may come into his own over longer distances
runners_data.spotlight: 13,000euros yearling; by Dubawi Legend; dam 7f 2yo winner (RPR 64), half-sister to winners Skeaping (1m2f Flat/2m hurdle), Time Najd (KSA 1m1f/1m2f) and Windy Cove (2m hurdle); pedigree suggests he may come into his own over longer distances.

runners_data.name: Katie's Knight
runners_data.comment: Early foal; stable has its share of 2yo winners and Rossa Ryan is a positive booking
runners_data.spotlight: £15,000 yearling; by Cotai Glory; dam placed 7f/1m AW (RPR 65), half-sister to French winners Harmless (7f 2yo/1m2f Listed), Ghabnah (1m) and Samuraj (6f-1m); early foal, already gelded; stable has its share of 2yo winners and Rossa Ryan is a positive booking.

runners_data.name: Stay On Tab
runners_data.comment: £5,000 yearling; has plenty of stamina on the dam's side of his pedigree; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: £5,000 yearling; by Harry Angel; dam 7f-1m3f maiden (RPR 68), closely related to 7f-2m2f Flat/2m4f hurdle winner Flint Hill, out of 1m6f winner; has plenty of stamina on the dam's side of his pedigree; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Magical El
runners_data.comment: Cost more than most of these and makes some appeal on pedigree; worth a market check
runners_data.spotlight: 42,000euros yearling; Make Believe half-sister to Listed-placed 7f winner Asian Daze (including 2yo; RPR 109); dam dual bumper winner, out of unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Habaayib; cost more than most of these and makes some appeal on pedigree; worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Midnight Curfew
runners_data.comment: Early foal; closely related to a 5f/6f 2yo winner; plausible pedigree for a race like this
runners_data.spotlight: 39,000euros yearling; early foal; closely related to 5f/6f 2yo winner Where's Clare (RPR 85); dam French Listed-placed 6f 2yo winner (97), half-sister to Qatari 1m2f Listed winner Emperor Maximus; has a plausible pedigree for a race of this nature.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.comment: £20,000 yearling; stable operates at around 7% with its 2yos; watch the market
runners_data.spotlight: £20,000 yearling; half-sister to French Listed-placed 6.5f/7f winner Summer Sail (RPR 102); dam unraced half-sister to 6f-1m winner Beau Jardine, out of Listed-placed 7f/1m winner; stable operates at around 7% with its 2yos; watch the market.

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny
runners_data.comment: 19,000gns yearling; first 2yo runner of the season for a very capable Newmarket yard
runners_data.spotlight: 19,000gns yearling; by Ardad; dam 1m AW 2yo winner (RPR 56), closely related to winners Maftoon (1m/1m1f) and Overpriced Mixer (7f/1m Flat and 2m hurdle); first 2yo runner of the season for a very capable Newmarket yard; must be respected.

runners_data.name: The Kalonji Man
runners_data.comment: Green when well held on last week's debut; no surprise at all to see him fare much better
runners_data.spotlight: Too green to do himself justice in last week's Brocklesby (won by a stablemate), beating only one home after a slow start; however, on paper that was a much stronger race than this one, and it would be no surprise at all to see him figure much more prominently with the run behind him.

races.name: Livescore Bet A Total Betting Experience Handicap

runners_data.name: Wheels Of Fire
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning to 5f having shown competitive pace in this trip previously, Sean Levey booking suggests strong chance
runners_data.comment: Most handicaps over 6f but fair mark and two good thirds in 5f races at Goodwood last year
runners_data.spotlight: Has spent most of his handicapping life over 6f, as when winning at Windsor in August, but he didn't lack for pace when close up in competitive 5f handicaps at Goodwood (good and heavy) last year; can come on for recent front-running AW return; has prospects for trainer who's 4-13 here.

runners_data.name: The Bell Conductor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner well-treated on current mark but AW form uninspiring, first-time visor adds tactical angle
runners_data.comment: Dropped 19lb since last spring but treading water now and questions remain
runners_data.spotlight: Ought to be well treated off a 19lb lower mark than last spring but he's been treading water on the AW this winter; made the running last time out (first-time visor, now goes in cheekpieces); questions linger.

runners_data.name: Al Hussar
runners_data.note: Prominent type who handles different surfaces well, 155-day break raises fitness concerns despite past form after rests
runners_data.comment: Acts on all ground; four 5f wins; took time to find his form in 2025; possibly other days
runners_data.spotlight: Copes well with different ground surfaces; all four wins at 5f but although he has won after a short break he took time to find his form in 2025; usually wears blinkers nowadays but not this time; possibly other days.

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to turf where he's shown his best form, healthy handicap mark after disappointing AW runs
runners_data.comment: Low-key AW season for new yard but on a healthy mark and ran well over C&D in August
runners_data.spotlight: Has not distinguished himself on Newcastle AW for new yard but returns to turf on a healthy mark; second to Ziggy's Triton over C&D (good) in August and has big turnaround at the weights; drawn widest but revival on the cards.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Prominent type off since November but has strong course record and reappearance form here previously
runners_data.comment: Good 2nd over C&D on return in 2025; C&D winner in August; now 2lb lower
runners_data.spotlight: Off since November but he was a very good runner-up on his reappearance over C&D last April (good; has won on soft) and later won here in August; lost his way subsequently but he's 2lb lower than the summer win and looks a likely type for this race.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with limited handicap experience, 186-day absence and 5-pound claiming jockey add complexity
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo; creditable close third over C&D in sole 5f start; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Just five handicap runs under his young belt, doing well to get as close as he did after a very slow start in the first of them; raced at mostly that 6f trip after and had to be chivvied along early in sole 5f run, when a close C&D third; nevertheless looks worth another go at 5f and not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Zarzyni
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with excellent course record including winning this race last year, now 2lb lower in the weights
runners_data.comment: Strong C&D record with three wins, including this race last year; primed to go well
runners_data.spotlight: Below best on latest course start in October but has a strong C&D record otherwise, three wins include this race (good to soft) last year; now 2lb lower and primed for a good run if he avoids trouble in running.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Triton
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose mark has been torpedoed by recent AW wins, needs to prove effectiveness on slower ground
runners_data.comment: 1-2 over C&D; 12lb higher than latest turf run following AW wins; may yet improve on grass
runners_data.spotlight: Winner of one of two C&D starts (good; has more to prove on slower) in August; two AW wins in December torpedoed his mark and he's 12lb higher than his latest turf run in October but he isn't a forlorn hope to transfer the winter improvement back to grass; the less rain the better.

runners_data.name: Arnhem
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran who showed good turf form in autumn including course second, looks to have conditions to suit
runners_data.comment: Made a winning yard debut in the autumn, later close up over C&D; tough off current mark
runners_data.spotlight: Good turf spell in the autumn included a winning yard debut at Haydock (good) and a close second over C&D (soft); has run well on AW since but looks to have his share of weight; trainer runs five and won this in 2024.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who's been prolific on AW but overall track record doesn't inspire confidence
runners_data.comment: Prolific winner, latest on AW in March; plenty to find on most C&D efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific winner, most recently on Wolverhampton AW last month; finished a respectable sixth of 12 in this race last year but overall track record doesn't scream course specialist and he needs a lot to go right.

runners_data.name: Thecoffeepoddotco
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader who can dictate pace, 0-7 on turf but none in handicaps, recent AW form encouraging
runners_data.comment: In good form on AW; needs a bit more back on turf but track should suit and fitness a plus
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 on turf but none of them were in handicaps and she's proved consistent on AW since, winning two 5f Lingfield races at the start of the year; needs a bit more for the return to turf, especially if the ground eases, but sharp tracks clearly suit and her fitness is a plus; yard also runs Wheels Of Fire.

runners_data.name: Classy Al
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong 5f record on good ground but often slow away from stalls, 186-day break concerns
runners_data.comment: Good 3rd in the 2024 running but slow starts have often counted against him over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Won three 5f handicaps (all on good) last summer; finished a good third to a stablemate in the 2024 running but he's often none too bright at the stalls, which has counted against him over C&D, and he may need this anyway.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with four wins last season but 227-day absence makes fitness questionable despite yard form
runners_data.comment: Four sprint wins in 2025; may yet continue improvement but off since August
runners_data.spotlight: Four sprint wins in 2025 on good to firm and good (also acts on good to soft) and she would have been close up in a Racing League race at Windsor in August but for some serious interference; not seen after one later run that month; improvement may well continue in 2026.

races.paceDynamic: Thecoffeepoddotco is the sole confirmed front-runner in this large field, meaning she can dictate terms without early pressure over this minimum trip. The Bell Conductor, Al Hussar, Pop Star, Curious Rover, and Ziggy's Triton all possess prominent tendencies but none are compulsive pace-forcers, likely settling behind the leader in the early stages. With a sustainable tempo likely through the first half on soft ground, this sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses to deliver their finishing kicks. The race shape strongly favours horses with finishing speed who can stay out of trouble in the large field and unleash late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate and the field stays together into the straight
scenarios.body: The soft ground will aid stamina and allow closers to wind up their runs effectively while prominent horses tire in the conditions. Multiple hold-up horses can deliver telling challenges in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Thecoffeepoddotco sets steady fractions and one prominent runner tracks her perfectly
scenarios.body: The leader and her closest pursuer can establish a decisive break turning for home before the hold-up horses can organise their challenges. This scenario suits horses with tactical pace who don't need to come from too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Thecoffeepoddotco gets uncontested easy fractions and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: Her recent AW form suggests she has the pace to steal a march if allowed to coast through gentle splits, potentially holding off late challengers on the testing ground. The lack of early pace pressure becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners track Thecoffeepoddotco closely creating a slow crawl
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair with positioning crucial, favouring horses drawn well who can get first run and those with a sharp turn of foot rather than sustained finishers.

Multiple Jim Goldie runners create stable complications with Arnhem, Montezuma, Water Of Leith, Classy Al and Woohoo all represented
